# 0.22.0 — 4 November 2026

Minor release on 0.21.0. This release is for the editor: the opentide VS Code extension ([`opentidehq.opentide`](https://marketplace.visualstudio.com/items?itemName=opentidehq.opentide)) ships its first release with it, and its catalogue, graph, relations and deploy-plan views run on two new commands, `opentide --json info catalog`, the catalogue and its relationships in one document, and `opentide serve`, which answers CLI commands from one warm process. `setup vscode` recommends the extension and stops mapping opentide's schemas for the YAML extension. The install is smaller, since `pip install opentide` no longer installs pandas or numpy, and Windows on Arm installs a wheel with the engine compiled in. `deploy --uuid` and `--file`, `setup --plan`, progress events and each platform's tenants in `info` are new. The engine is [language-server 0.10.0](https://github.com/opentidehq/language-server/releases/tag/v0.10.0).

## Upgrade

```bash
pip install opentide==0.22.0
export OPENTIDE_REPO_ROOT=/path/to/detection-repo
opentide validate --strict
opentide setup vscode --settings --no-generate   # drops the yaml.schemas mappings earlier releases wrote
opentide generate snippets                       # snippets for the extension's object files
```

Then install the recommended [opentide extension](https://marketplace.visualstudio.com/items?itemName=opentidehq.opentide) and reload the window.

| Before | Now |
|--------|-----|
| `setup vscode` recommended `redhat.vscode-yaml` and mapped object files to opentide's schemas in `.vscode/settings.json` (`yaml.schemas`) | it recommends `opentidehq.opentide`, whose language server checks object files, and writes no `yaml.schemas`; `opentide setup vscode --settings --no-generate` removes the mappings earlier releases wrote and keeps every other setting. A YAML extension still mapped to the schemas reports every problem a second time, which `doctor`'s `vscode_settings` now warns about |
| Snippets had `scope: "yaml"` | `scope: "yaml,opentide-yaml"`, so `tide-rule`, `tide-sentinel` and the others complete in the extension's object files too; run `opentide generate snippets` |
| `pip install opentide` installed pandas and numpy | neither is installed, and no other dependency pulls them in. Code that imports them because opentide installed them must add them to its own requirements. Deployed configurations are unchanged: deploy flattens tenant modifiers with its own function, which gives the keys `pandas.json_normalize` gave |
| A query finding over several lines had an `end_column` one past its first character, on its first line | `end_column` is the column after its last character, on the new `end_line`. A script that reads `end_column` as a column of `line` reads `end_line` first; a one-line finding is unchanged |
| A tenant setup value `${VAR}` resolved only for Elastic's `api_key` and Sysdig's `api_token`, and any `$text` was looked up as the variable `text` | `$NAME` and `${NAME}` resolve on every platform, and another value that starts with `$` is a literal (a variable of exactly that name is still read, with a warning to rename it). Re-run `opentide setup ci <provider> --yes` so the live query job guards the same names |
| On Windows on Arm, `pip install opentide` compiled opentide from its sdist, which needs Rust | it installs a wheel. Use CPython 3.11 or later and `pip install --only-binary cryptography opentide==0.22.0` (cryptography's last Windows on Arm wheel is 46.0.3) |

It is a minor because it adds commands (`info catalog`, `serve`) and features, changes the files `setup vscode` and `generate snippets` write, changes the `end_column` that scripts read, and drops two dependencies.

## Added

- **`opentide --json info catalog`: the catalogue and its relationships in one document** ([#749](https://github.com/opentidehq/opentide/issues/749)). One row per threat, objective and rule (path, metadata, platform blocks, deployment-state bindings, own and inherited techniques, tactics and actors, and a `load_error` for a file that did not load), the `covers`, `implements`, `parent`, `chains`, `technique` and `logsource` edges with `missing: true` for a dangling reference, the signals, and the Enterprise ATT&CK matrix. A 500-rule workspace answers in about 1.3 s.
- **`opentide serve`: CLI commands in one warm process, for editors** ([#750](https://github.com/opentidehq/opentide/issues/750)). JSON-RPC 2.0 on stdio: a `run {argv, cwd?, env?}` request answers with exactly the document `opentide --json <argv>` prints, and its exit code, without restarting Python or rebuilding the registry (a repeat `validate --file` at 500 rules: about 0.3 s instead of 1.6 s). One server serves a multi-root window; `invalidate`, `$/cancelRequest` (exit `130`, failure code `interrupted`) and `progress` notifications are part of the protocol.
- **`opentide setup --plan`, and the whole wizard as one command** ([#751](https://github.com/opentidehq/opentide/issues/751)). `--plan` on `setup` and every subcommand lists each file a step would write or remove, and writes nothing; `setup --yes` with the same flags writes exactly those files. `--mcp`, `--skills`, `--plugin`, `--hooks` and `--env` answer the wizard's remaining questions.
- **`opentide deploy --uuid` and `--file` select the rules a run reads** ([#753](https://github.com/opentidehq/opentide/issues/753)), in place of the git-diff default, so `deploy --dry-run --uuid <rule>` plans and renders only that rule. A value that selects no rule fails the run, naming it in `unmatched`.
- **`opentide --json info` lists each platform's tenants** ([#754](https://github.com/opentidehq/opentide/issues/754)): `name`, `description`, `strategies`, `manual`, and each `$VAR` the tenant's setup references with whether it is set. A value is never printed.
- **Progress events for editors and scripts** ([#756](https://github.com/opentidehq/opentide/issues/756)). With `OPENTIDE_PROGRESS=json`, `generate`, `validate`, `validate query`, `deploy --dry-run` and `query` write one ASCII JSON object per line on stderr as they go. Stdout still holds exactly one document.
- **Every `validate`, `validate query` and `lint` finding carries `end_line`** ([#755](https://github.com/opentidehq/opentide/issues/755)), and SARIF regions carry `endLine`.
- **A wheel for Windows on Arm** (`cp310-abi3-win_arm64`, [#748](https://github.com/opentidehq/opentide/issues/748)), with the engine compiled in; a release is refused without one.

## Changed

- **The engine is language-server 0.10.0, from crates.io**: a placeholder query `opentide new` leaves (`...` under `# opentide:placeholder`) is no longer reported as a parse error in the editor, `opentide/catalog` serves editors the workspace index with each object's references and follows unsaved edits, and a folder deleted, created or moved under `objects/` is read again.
- **`pip install opentide` no longer installs pandas or numpy** ([#747](https://github.com/opentidehq/opentide/issues/747)). They were most of the size of every install, for one code path. A `[[modifiers]]` entry with an empty `modifications` table, which failed with `IndexError`, now changes nothing.
- **`opentide setup vscode` sets up the opentide VS Code extension** ([#752](https://github.com/opentidehq/opentide/issues/752)): it recommends `opentidehq.opentide`, writes no `yaml.schemas` and removes the mappings earlier releases wrote; snippets are scoped to `yaml,opentide-yaml`; `doctor`'s `vscode_settings` checks the recommendation; and `setup mcp --vscode` says when the extension already provides the MCP server (`"extension_mcp": true`).
- **A query finding over several lines ends where it ends** ([#755](https://github.com/opentidehq/opentide/issues/755)): its `end_column` is on `end_line`, after its last character.

## Fixed

- **`deploy`, `validate query --changed` and `lint --changed` in a repository with no commit yet no longer fail with `b'HEAD'`** ([#769](https://github.com/opentidehq/opentide/pull/769)). Outside CI nothing has changed, so they report it with a warning; in CI the message is readable, and a missing git ref is named in a sentence.
- **A tenant setup value written `${VAR}` resolves on every platform, and `doctor` names the variable** ([#766](https://github.com/opentidehq/opentide/pull/766), [#768](https://github.com/opentidehq/opentide/pull/768)). A secret that only starts with `$` is used as written, and the generated live query job guards the same names.
- **`info` counts a file whose UUID another file also uses as a load error** ([#766](https://github.com/opentidehq/opentide/pull/766)), so `--strict` fails as `validate` does.
- **Interrupting `opentide generate` no longer leaves an empty schema that breaks every later command** ([#766](https://github.com/opentidehq/opentide/pull/766), [#768](https://github.com/opentidehq/opentide/pull/768)): schemas are written atomically, and one that cannot be parsed is skipped with a warning and rewritten.
- **`setup skills` keeps the files you added to a skill's folder, and no longer deletes the skills when `.claude/skills` links to `.agents/skills`** ([#767](https://github.com/opentidehq/opentide/pull/767), [#768](https://github.com/opentidehq/opentide/pull/768)).
- **`setup vscode` reads files saved with a byte-order mark, and keeps the comments, layout and line endings of `.vscode/settings.json` and `extensions.json`** ([#767](https://github.com/opentidehq/opentide/pull/767), [#768](https://github.com/opentidehq/opentide/pull/768)). A file it cannot parse or edit in place is left unchanged, with a warning.

See the [CHANGELOG](https://github.com/opentidehq/opentide/blob/development/CHANGELOG.md) for every change.

## Verify

```bash
pip install opentide==0.22.0
python -c "import opentide; print(opentide.__version__)"   # 0.22.0
opentide doctor                                             # analysis_engine: language server 0.10.0
```
